statements.t: The PROTO project is intended to support the development of novel interventional strategies for knee osteoarthritis, including a Phase I clinical study of our PLX-PAD cells for the treatment of mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis.

In addition, on September 11, 2026, we filed a new registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-298867) (the “Pending S-3”), with the SEC, which, upon being declared effective by the SEC, is intended to replace the existing shelf registration statement.

Pursuant to the Advance Subscription Agreement, Chutzpah Holdings agreed to pay us an advance amount of $1,250,000 (the “Advance Amount”), which was received on June 16, 2026, and will be used for working capital and general corporate purposes.

The August Offering closed on August 28, 2026, and the Company received gross proceeds in the amount of $3.3 million, which it intends to use for corporate development, general purposes and working capital.

Upon completion of the transactions contemplated by the agreement, we will own 50% of ZEO’s outstanding shares, with rights to acquire additional equity interests pursuant to the terms of the agreement.

The proceeds from the EIB Finance Agreement were intended to support our R&D in the European Union to further advance our regenerative cell therapy platform, and to bring the products in our pipeline to market.

As part of this collaboration, novel Chimeric Switch Receptors, developed by Professor Cohen, head of laboratory of tumor immunology and immunotherapy at Bar-Ilan University, will be integrated into our CAR-MAIT cell therapy platform to enhance tumor specificity and therapeutic efficacy.
The goal of the PROTO project is to utilize our PLX-PAD cells in a Phase I/II study for the treatment of mild to moderate knee osteoarthritis.
An amount of approximately €500,000 (approximately $540,000) is a direct grant that will be allocated to us.
We do not anticipate generating any significant revenues from sales of products in the next twelve months.

There are no assurances, however, that we will be successful in obtaining an adequate level of financing needed for the long-term development and commercialization of our products, or any financing at all.
These activities may require more time, financing and other resources than anticipated, disrupt existing operations and divert management attention.
We or ZEO may not have sufficient funding to complete the contemplated activities, and we may not realize anticipated revenues, efficiencies or other benefits.
Insufficient funding, manufacturing capacity, market acceptance or regulatory progress could delay or prevent commercialization and reduce the value of our investment and royalty income.

Our ability to pursue alternative partners will be constrained by exclusivity and applicable remediation procedures, and conversion to non-exclusive rights may not promptly restore lost opportunities.
We will also incur costs for our own technical support and other obligations.

Although we expect to own 50% of ZEO’s outstanding shares at closing and have rights to nominate four of seven directors, director appointments are subject to approval requirements, and ZEO’s management will retain responsibility for day to day operations.
These issues may adversely impact our ability to obtain the full benefits we expect from the transactions contemplated by the Partnership Agreement.

Depending on the arrangements ultimately agreed with the IIA in connection with the license to manufacture and commercialize our products in the United States, we may incur payments or other financial obligations that could materially reduce the anticipated economic benefits of the transactions contemplated by the Partnership Agreement.
